newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable on liquidity, swaps down.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable on liquidity, swaps down.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in early trading on Thursday on sufficient liquidity, with short-term swap rates seen easing, dealers said.
One European bank dealer said the trading range in the spot market remained tight due to a lack of fresh market factors.
"The spot rate has hovered at the current levels for several days and we expect the rate to remain so in the next few days," he said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,431.50/32.00 at 0230 GMT against an opening of 2,431.00/32.00.
Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,431.00/31.50 and 2,431.00/31.50, respectively.
Another dealer said some Singaporean operators were seen focussing on short-term swaps, which were easing as rupiah liquidity was likely to remain sufficient in the near term.
He said relatively sufficient liquidity supply on a day-to-day basis partly helped the downtrend in the short-term swaps rates.
The central bank, Bank Indonesia, for example, supplied some 262 billion rupiah temporarily on the money market in early trading, he said.
Overnight swaps fell to -0.05/par points from an opening of 0.15/0.25 points, while tom/next fell to 0.40/0.45 from an opening of 0.75/0.85 points.
One-month swaps were at 14.00/14.50, two at 27.50/28.00, three at 42.50/43.50 and six at 85.50/87.00 points.
Dealers said the spot rupiah rate was likely to remain moving between 2432.00 to 2432.50 the rest of the day as operators expected the central bank to raise its fixing rate later today.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,424/2,616 and its conversion band at 2,424/2,472 on Wednesday.
